title: The Return of the Lost Mitten
skyStory: The moon is down to a thin ribbon, still curled up in Scorpio and refusing to leave. Scorpio likes secrets, and tonight it is sitting on a big one: something lost in December is ready to be found. The moon will not say what. It only taps its nose twice and drifts behind a cloud shaped like a kettle.

reading: Somewhere in your world there is a single mitten, glove or sock that lost its partner in the holiday chaos. Today it comes home. You will find it in a coat pocket you swear you checked, and you will hold it up like a trophy. The Tiger roars quietly. Victory is victory.

Later, the [[Knight of Pentacles]] trots by and suggests you finish one tiny chore you have been dodging, like the burnt-out bulb in the hallway. Do it before 4 pm. The light that comes on afterward is symbolic, obviously, and also just useful. Tell somebody about it with far too much drama.
joel.mission: Narrate one boring chore today like a nature documentary host, in a hushed voice, for at least thirty seconds.
joel.omen: A lone mitten on a fence post. It means someone in your life is waiting to be found and would love a message.

reading: The shore is frozen at the edges today, lace ice along the rocks, and you will feel like a detective. Something is off in a small, delightful way. Maybe a picture frame tilted. Maybe a word in an email spelled like a sneeze. The Wood Rat in you cannot leave it alone, and should not.

So here is the plan: fix one tiny wrongness with full ceremony. Straighten the frame. Correct the typo. Then announce it to the room, even if the room is empty. The [[Eight of Swords]] is a cage made of thoughts, and nothing bends its bars like doing one small thing completely.
nancy.mission: Find one thing that is slightly crooked, straighten it, and then bow to it.
nancy.omen: Lace ice shaped like a letter of the alphabet. It is the initial of someone who will make you laugh this week.

together.text: Hide a tiny surprise for the other person to discover later: a silly voice note scheduled for tomorrow morning, a doodle tucked in a shared document, a riddle with no answer. Do not mention it. Let the universe handle the delivery.

game.intro: A mitten came home today after weeks at sea. In honour of its return, Saturn wants your finest lost-and-found lies.
game.prompt: Three things you lost and later found again. One of them never happened.
